title: ERA/EOB Reconciliation and Payment Posting
summary: Accurate and timely payment posting from electronic remittance advices is essential for maintaining clean AR and identifying underpayments.
objectives: Distinguish between ERA (835) and paper EOB and explain how each is processed
Describe the payment posting workflow including contractual adjustment posting
Explain how to identify and pursue payer underpayments

content_blocks.body:
**Electronic Remittance Advice (ERA / 835):** The HIPAA-standard electronic transaction that payers send to providers detailing claim adjudication — payment amounts, contractual adjustments, and denial codes. ERAs enable automated payment posting and significantly reduce manual processing.

**Explanation of Benefits (EOB):** The paper or PDF equivalent of an ERA, sent to both the provider and patient. EOBs are processed manually, increasing labor costs and error rates.

Best-practice organizations achieve 90%+ ERA adoption rates, limiting paper EOB processing to payers that do not support 835 transactions.
content_blocks.heading: ERA vs. EOB

content_blocks.body:
Payer underpayments — where the payer pays less than the contracted rate — are common and often overlooked. Causes include:

- Incorrect fee schedule loaded in the payer's system
- Modifier not recognized or applied incorrectly
- Bundling of services that should be paid separately
- Wrong DRG assignment on inpatient claims

Payment variance analysis compares expected payment (based on contract) to actual payment for every claim. Organizations with automated contract management systems recover 1–3% of net revenue from identified underpayments.
content_blocks.heading: Identifying Underpayments

content_blocks.body: Payment posting must occur within 24–48 hours of receipt to maintain accurate AR visibility. Delayed posting makes it impossible to identify truly outstanding claims versus paid claims not yet posted — leading to duplicate follow-up calls, wasted staff time, and inaccurate financial reporting.
content_blocks.title: Timely Posting is Critical
